Title: Diagnosis
Details:
The failing test case `testCOMPRESS335` tries to read from the archive "COMPRESS-335.tar". The current bug report indicates the failure is due to checksum failing when the checksum field in the TAR header is right aligned with zero padding instead of the expected format, causing the last two digits of the checksum to be lost.

Looking into the code, the checksum verification is done in the static method `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum(byte[] header)`. This method calculates a stored checksum by reading up to 6 octal digits from the checksum field in the header (offset 148, length 8 bytes as per `CHKSUM_OFFSET=148` and `CHKSUMLEN=8`). The code uses a counter `digits` to limit adding digits to the checksum to only the first 6 octal digits. If a non-octal digit is found after starting to parse digits, it stops parsing further digits.

The bug report points out that some TAR files have a checksum field that is right aligned with zero-padding to the left, and missing the trailing NULL and SPACE terminator. The existing code extracts only the first 6 octal digits starting from offset 148 but assumes that any space characters are after those digits (to replace bytes with spaces when summing).

Because of this limitation, stored checksum parsing ignores any digits beyond the first 6, so right aligned checksums (with zeros padding the beginning and the real digits at the end) are misparsed, resulting in losing the last two digits and an invalid checksum calculation.

The comments on `verifyCheckSum` state that this is a heuristic method, and it tries to account for different TAR implementations, but the current implementation does not handle the right aligned checksum with leading zeros adequately.

Hence, the root cause of the bug is that `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum` only parses the first 6 octal digits of the checksum field from the start of the checksum field and stops, which fails on checksums that are right aligned and padded with zeros on the left, causing a legitimate checksum to be treated as invalid.

The test `testCOMPRESS335` triggers this by loading a TAR archive with such a checksum format, causing the checksum verification to fail.

The problem lies in the logic inside the loop at lines 599-608 in `verifyCheckSum`. It stops collecting checksum digits after the first 6 digits encountered starting at offset 148, ignoring any further digits or the possibly missing terminator format.

Recent bug reports about directory sizes or BSD long names are unrelated to this checksum parsing issue and can be disregarded.

In conclusion, the bug was triggered by the test providing a TAR archive with a right aligned checksum field format that `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum` does not properly handle due to its limitation of only parsing the first 6 octal digits from the beginning of the checksum field.

The fix should improve checksum parsing in `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum` to support leading zero padded right aligned checksums instead of only reading the first 6 digits from the start.

The failing test's `getStreamFor` method simply loads the input stream for the test archive and hands it to the TAR archive input stream, which then calls the checksum verification internally.

This confirms the issue lies within `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum`.

---

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
